overlayEdits.reason: The ADR-016 core edit: the friend class AeroraVehicleFactGroupRegistrar declaration and the AERORA_VEHICLE_FACTGROUP_FRIENDSHIP compile definition. The only one of these five that carries Decision_Content, and the only one whose content a rule already holds -- adr-016-pair reads both halves against DG-TLM, so this entry records that the reach exists and that rule records whether it is applied. Requirement 7 criterion 17 names Tab 1 as the owner whose signature the edit requires.

The regression guard for the ADR-012 command-authorization hook, registered by test/Vehicle/CMakeLists.txt as Unit Vehicle. It sits in the upstream test tree because half of what it asserts is that stock QGC is unaffected: the default hook authorizes and never dereferences its Vehicle pointer, which needs the upstream QGCCorePlugin base implementation rather than an overlay type. The rest stubs the identity provider, the role resolver, the policy and the audit sink and asserts the chain denies by default. It names overlay types and carries no withheld value.

A comment and nothing else: it points at the AeroraSceneAttachmentUITest registration in aerora/CMakeLists.txt so a reader of the upstream test macro can find where the overlay registers a suite that macro does not. Recorded because overlay-isolation matches an identifier wherever it appears, which is deliberate over-approximation -- a rule that exempted comments would exempt the place a reach is most easily hidden. Withdrawing the comment is the removal this entry would then report.

The Linux CI leg for the overlay. It configures the build with CUSTOMCLASS=AeroraCorePlugin and AERORA_VEHICLE_FACTGROUP_FRIENDSHIP, and asserts that AeroraSceneAttachmentUITest is registered as an Integration test, which is why this leg names a suite and the Windows one does not. A new file rather than an edit to an upstream workflow, so it carries no rebase conflict.

The Windows CI leg for the overlay, configuring CUSTOMCLASS=AeroraCorePlugin and AERORA_VEHICLE_FACTGROUP_FRIENDSHIP. It names no suite: the scene-attachment test is registered off Windows, so this leg has no registration to assert. A new file rather than an edit to an upstream workflow.

hazards.statement: Manual control input carried on a path through a general-purpose operating system has no bounded worst-case latency. A host that stalls, swaps or schedules the station late does not fall back to a slower path: it delivers stick positions late or not at all, and an operator holding the sticks has no way to tell which of those is happening.
hazards.severity: loss of manual control authority in flight
hazards.mitigation: Manual control input reaches the Flight_Controller directly and never traverses the Aerora_Station. The station issues a Manual_Authority_Grant which the Flight_Controller itself enforces, which carries an expiry, which requires refresh to stay in force, and which expires without refresh when the link drops. That makes the station a single point of authority rather than a single point of control: a stalled host withdraws permission to fly manually and never withdraws the ability to.

hazards.statement: A hexacopter at hover draws kilowatts, and an interruption of the tether DC bus long enough to brown out an ESC is long enough to stop the motors. No software path meets that deadline: not the Aerora_Station over a link, and not the Flight_Controller in firmware.
hazards.severity: loss of all thrust in flight
hazards.mitigation: The transfer from tether supply to onboard battery is performed by the power hardware of the aircraft without a software decision, and the Aerora_Station is forbidden from participating in it. The contribution of the station is everything around the transfer and never the transfer itself: reporting the onboard reserve before flight, reporting a failover as a degraded flight rather than as a routine mode change, and reporting the flight time the battery sustains. Requirement 11 criterion 2 is the record of that design and this entry carries it.
